The <ns0:hi>Lutherans</ns0:hi> have another notion, as<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cribing an <ns0:hi>Omnipresence,</ns0:hi> even to the humane Nature of Christ, because of its personal Union with the Divine Na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ture; and so affirm that Christs Humane Nature while it was on Earth, was also substantially in Heaven; as on the other side, they are as stiff in maintaining that, altho Christs Humane Nature be now in Heaven, yet it is also on Earth really and essentially present, wherever the Sacrament of the Lords Supper is Administred; but this is to ascribe a Body unto Christ, which indeed is no Body, according to any notion we have of a Body.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 ¶ And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">The History of the lifting up of the Serpent in the Wilderness, we have, <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 21.8, 9. the people being stung with fiery Serpents, as a righteous Judgment of God for their sins, as a merciful remedy, God commanded <ns0:hi>Moses,</ns0:hi> v. 8. <ns0:hi>Make thee a fiery Serpent,</ns0:hi> [that is, the Image or Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />presentation of one of those fiery Serpents], <ns0:hi>and set it upon a pole, and it shall come to pass, that every one that is bitten, when he looketh upon it, shall live</ns0:hi>; this brazen Ser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pent in the Wilderness was a lively Type of Jesus Christ. Our Saviour having before spoken of the <ns0:hi>New Birth</ns0:hi> as necessary to those who shall be saved; here comes to shew it in the causes, and instanceth first in the meritorious, then in the instrumental cause, the meritorious cause was his Death; he saith, That look as the Serpent was lift up in the Wilderness:</ns0:note>: even so must the Son of man be lifted up <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">So he, who was the Son of man must be lifted up; that is, <ns0:hi>dye upon the Cross</ns0:hi>: the Phrase is used twice more in this Gospel, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 8.28. and 12.32, 34. an allusion doubtless to this Type. Yet Mr. <ns0:hi>Calvin</ns0:hi> thinks the <ns0:hi>lifted up</ns0:hi> here, more properly interpreted of the <ns0:hi>Doctrine of the Gospel,</ns0:hi> and by the Preaching of it; and others ap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ply it to <ns0:hi>Christs ascension into Heaven</ns0:hi>; and this he tells <ns0:hi>Nicodemus</ns0:hi> must be, for the fulfilling the Scripture, and the Counsels of his Father.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 That whosoever believeth in him, should not perish, but <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Vers. 36. Chap. 6.47.</ns0:note> have eternal life <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Here our Lord openeth the <ns0:hi>Instrumental cause</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Iu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stification</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Salvation,</ns0:hi> that is, believing <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 
                     <ns0:hi>in him.</ns0:hi> It is one thing to <ns0:hi>believe him</ns0:hi> as a <ns0:hi>Teacher,</ns0:hi> another thing to believe <ns0:hi>in him</ns0:hi> as a <ns0:hi>Saviour.</ns0:hi> The Object of the first is a Proposition; we believe a Person when we assent and give credit to what he saith, because he saith it. The Object of the latter, is the Person and Merits of the Mediator. As the looking up to the brazen Serpen healed the Person, not by any <ns0:hi>physical Operation,</ns0:hi> but from the goodness of God, as it was an act of Obedience to the Divine Institution for that end: So neither doth Faith in the Mediator justifie and obtain pardon for any Soul from any meritorious vertue in that act, but from Gods gracious Ordination, that so it shall be; he hath so ordain<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed, that whosoever should rest upon Christ, and receive him by Faith as his Mediator and Saviour, should not pe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rish, but live for ever. There are other things besides <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi> necessary to Salvation, such are Repentance, Love, and new Obedience; nor is Faith onely mentioned, because they are ingredients into it; but because <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi> is the root of all those, and that from which they must necessarily slow; for it is as impossible that any should truly hope, and trust in, and rest upon Christ for that life which he hath onely promi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sed to those that obey him; as it is impossible that any should indeed trust in, and rest upon a man who hath promised a reward upon a condition, for that reward, without any care to fulfil that condition. But by this and other places, where Faith alone in Christ is mentioned as necessary to Salvation; <ns0:hi>Nicodemus</ns0:hi> was taught, that no Obedience to the works of the Law without this Faith in the Me<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />diator, would bring the Soul to eternal Life and Salva<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 ¶ <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Joh. 4.9.</ns0:note> For God so loved the world <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">For God the Father, who is the Lord of all, Debtor to none, sufficient to himself, so loved the <ns0:hi>World,</ns0:hi> that is, <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> as well as <ns0:hi>Iews.</ns0:hi> There is a great contest about the Signification of the term, betwixt those who contend for or against the point of <ns0:hi>Vniversal Redemption</ns0:hi>; but cer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tain it is, that from this term no more can be solidly con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cluded, than from the term <ns0:hi>all</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>every,</ns0:hi> which in multi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tudes of places are taken in a restrained sense for many, or all of such a Nation or kind; as this term sometimes sig<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nifies all persons, so in 1 <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 2.2. the <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> in oppo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sition to the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi>; nor (admit that the World should sig<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nifie here every living Soul, in the place called the World) will any thing follow from it. It is proper enough to say, A man loved such a Family to such a degree, that he gave his Estate to it, tho he never intended such a thing to e<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />very Child or Branch of it; so as what is truth in that so vexed question, cannot be determined from any of these Universal terms; which must, when all is said or can be said, be expounded by what follows them, and by their reconcilableness to other Doctrines of Faith. God so loved the World</ns0:note>, that he
gave his onely begotten Son <ns0:note n="k," place="bottom">that he gave his Son to dye for a Sacrifice for their Sins, to dye in their stead, and give a Satisfaction for them to his Justice. And this Son was not any of his Sons <ns0:hi>by Adoption,</ns0:hi> but his <ns0:hi>onely begotten Son</ns0:hi>; not so called (as <ns0:hi>S<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>cinians</ns0:hi> would have it;) because of his singular Genera<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion of the Virgin without help of man, but from his eter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nal Generation, <ns0:hi>in whom the Gentiles should trust,</ns0:hi> Psal. 2.12. which none ought to do, but in God alone, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 6.13. <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 17.5.</ns0:note>: that whosoever be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieveth in him, should not perish, but have everlast<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing life <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>That whosoever,</ns0:hi> &c. The term [<ns0:hi>all</ns0:hi>] oc<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />curred, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 15. and is there spoken to; these words re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />strain the Universal term <ns0:hi>World,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>all</ns0:hi> tolet us know that Christ onely dyed for some in the World, viz. <ns0:hi>such as should believe in him.</ns0:hi> Some judge, not improbably, that Christ useth the term <ns0:hi>World,</ns0:hi> in this Verse in the same sense, as in 1 <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 2.2. Our Evangelist useth to take down the pride of the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> who dreamed that the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> came onely for the benefit of the Seed of <ns0:hi>Abraham</ns0:hi>; not for the Nations of the World, he onely came to destroy them, which notion also very well fitteth what we have in the next Verse.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:334" />17 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luk. 9.56. Chap. 5.45. and 8.15. and 12.47.</ns0:note> For God sent not his Son into the world, to condemn the world <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">The word we translate <ns0:hi>Condemn,</ns0:hi> is <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, signifies to <ns0:hi>Iudg,</ns0:hi> as well as to <ns0:hi>Condemn.</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> were mistaken in their proud conceit, that Christ came to Judge and de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stroy all those that were not of their Nation; thus <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 12.47. he saith, <ns0:hi>he came not to judge, but to save the world</ns0:hi>; <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>or is this contrary to what he saith, chap. 9.39. <ns0:hi>For judg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment am I come into this world</ns0:hi>; for that is <ns0:hi>ex accidenti,</ns0:hi> from the corruption of men, shutting their Eyes against the Light, and hardening their Hearts against the Offers and tenders of Divine Grace. Christ will come in his second coming to Condemn the World of unbelievers; but the ten<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dency of his coming,</ns0:note>: but that the world through him might be saved <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">was not for Condemnation, but to offer the Grace of the Gospel, and eternal Life and Salvati<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on to men in the World.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 ¶ <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 5.24. and 6.40, 47. and 20.31.</ns0:note> He that believeth on him, is not condem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ned <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Who so firmly, and steadily assenting to the Propo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sitions of the Gospel, revealing Jesus Christ as the onely and all-sufficient Saviour, commits the care of his Soul unto him, trusting and hoping in him alone for eternal Salvation, which no man can indeed do, without doing what in him lyeth to fulfil the condition upon which Christ hath promised Life and Salvation; that is, keeping the Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mandments of God, is exempted from Condemnation by the Law of Grace. But he that believes not the Doctrine of Christ, and does not upon the terms of the Gospel re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceive him for his Saviour, is already condemned for his obstinate Infidelity, which is the certain cause of Damna<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion; as we say of one mortally wounded, That he is a dead Man, tho he breathes for a while; and we speak in the same manner of a Malefactor, convicted and attainted of a Capital Crime, tho the Sentence be not Executed, because their Death is inevitable. The not believing in the onely Son of God, who is able to save to the utmost all that regu<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>arly trust in him, is such a contempt of the merciful, all-sufficient and sole means of Salvation, that 'tis absolutely necessary, and most just, that all those who refuse to be saved by him, should perish by themselves. From this Scrip<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ture arise two Questions, The first concerning <ns0:hi>the Hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thens,</ns0:hi> who never heard of Christ. The second concerning <ns0:hi>Infants,</ns0:hi> who dye before they come to years of Knowledg. As to the former, the Apostle hath determined, Rom. 2.12. <ns0:hi>As many as have sinned without the Law, shall also pe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rish without law.</ns0:hi> There is the same reason for those who sin without the Gospel; they shall not perish for not be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieving <ns0:hi>on him, of whom they have not heard,</ns0:hi> Rom. 10.14. but for not obeying such Revelation of the Divine Will as they had. The case of <ns0:hi>Infants</ns0:hi> is excluded from this Text, (speaking onely of adult Persons). It is certain, that so ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ny of them as belong to the <ns0:hi>Election of Grace,</ns0:hi> shall be <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>aved, and that by vertue of the Blood of Christ; but which way God brings them to Heaven, is a secret to us. Some from this Text have concluded, That unbelief is the onely damning Sin; which is no further true, than, That no Sin will damn that Soul which shall truly believe in the Lord Jesus Christ.</ns0:note>: but he that believeth not, is condemned al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ready <ns0:hi>p,</ns0:hi> because he hath not believed in the Name of the onely begotten Son of God <ns0:hi>q.</ns0:hi>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 And this is the condemnation, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 1.4, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, 10, 11.</ns0:note> that light is come into the world <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">This is the Reason, the Evidence and great Cause of Condemnation, That Light is come into the World<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> Christ is the Light, foretold by the Prophet, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 9.2. and 42.6. and 49.6. He is stiled in the beginning of this Gospel, the true Light, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 1.4. that is, hath in perfection all the excellent qua<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lities of Light; the Power to enlighten the minds of men in the Knowledg of saving Truth, to warm the Affections with the love of it, to revive the disconsolate, and to make the heavenly Seed of the Word, to flourish and fructifie in their lives; this light is come into the World, that signi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fies not onely his Incarnation, but his revealing the mer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ciful Counsel of God for our Salvation, which the clearest Spirits could never have discovered; he has open'd the way that leads to Eternal Life; but men loved Darkness rather than Light.</ns0:note>, and men loved dark<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness rather than light <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">They preferr'd, chose and adher'd to their Ignorance and Errors, before the Light of Life, the saving Knowledg of the Gospel. Their Ignorance is affected and voluntary, and no colour of excuse can be alledged for it; nay 'tis very culpable and guilty, by neglecting to receive instruction from the Son of God.</ns0:note>; because their deeds were evil <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">The vices and lusts of men are the works of Darkness, the fruits of their Ignorance and Errors; and they are so pleasant to the car<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nal corrupt Nature, that to enjoy them securely, they obsti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nately reject the Light of the Gospel; this aggravates their Sin and Sentence.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 For <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Job 24.13, 17.</ns0:note> every one that doeth evil <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">He that makes a trade of Sin, and doth Evil presump<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tuously, loving and delighting in it,</ns0:note>, hateth the light <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">doth not love the Light,</ns0:note>, neither cometh to the light <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">nor if he can avoid it, will come near it; for the Light is that which makes things Visible, and discovereth them. As it is of the nature of natural Light, to shew things to others as they are; and therefore Thieves, and A<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dulterers, and Drunkards, care not for the Light, but chuse the Darkness for their deeds of darkness, and come as little abroad in the Light, as they can, when they do them: So it is of the Nature of Christ and his Gospel, to discover mens errors, both as to the obtaining of Justification and Eternal Salvation, and the Errors also of mens Lives; and therefore men and women possessed of Errors in their Judg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ments, or delighting in a filthy Conversation, hate Christ and his Gospel; because that a discovering the right ways of God, discovereth the crookedness of their ways, opposite to the truths and ways of God.</ns0:note>, lest his deeds should be <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>disco<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vered or con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />victed.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> reproved <ns0:hi>y.</ns0:hi>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 But he that doeth truth <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Truth here, is put for true things. He who purposeth, designeth, and acteth nothing but what is just, and holy, and good, and what is consonant to the Will of God,</ns0:note>, cometh to the light <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">He is not afraid to bring his Notions and Actions to the Test of the Divine Rule, published by him, who is the true Light.</ns0:note>, that his deeds may be made manifest, that they are wrought in God <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">For he that desires what he doth may be made manifest, both to himself and others, that they are wrought <ns0:hi>in, with,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>according to, by,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>through</ns0:hi> God, (for the Particle <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> here used, is used in all these senses, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 7.39. <ns0:hi>Rev.</ns0:hi> 14.13.) Those works are said to be wrought in, with, by or through God, which tend to the Honour and Glory of God, as their end, and flow from him as their cause, which are done with his Strength and Assistance, and for his Honour and Glory.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 ¶ After these things <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Soon after our Saviour had had the forementioned con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ference with <ns0:hi>Nicodemus,</ns0:hi> which it is believed he had at <ns0:hi>Hierusalem,</ns0:hi> not (as some think) in <ns0:hi>Galilee</ns0:hi>; for then <ns0:hi>Nicodemus</ns0:hi> would hardly have come to him by Night;</ns0:note>, came Jesus and his disciples into the land of Judea <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">he came into the Land of <ns0:hi>Iudea</ns0:hi>; he had before been in the <ns0:hi>Province of Iudea,</ns0:hi> and in the <ns0:hi>Metropolis,</ns0:hi> or great City of <ns0:hi>Iudea,</ns0:hi> which was <ns0:hi>Hierusalem</ns0:hi>; but now he goeth into the <ns0:hi>Country of Iudea. Iudah</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Hierusalem</ns0:hi> are of<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ten mentioned distinctly. The chief City of a Country is oft distinguished from the Country, tho within the same Province and Tribe, see <ns0:hi>Iosh.</ns0:hi> 8.1. <ns0:hi>The King of Ai, his City and his Land,</ns0:hi> and in particular as to <ns0:hi>Hierusalem,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 11.14. and 20.17. and 36.23. <ns0:hi>Ezr.</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.1. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 5.17. and 6.17. Christ and his Disciples went into the Country-part of <ns0:hi>Iudea,</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, and there he <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap>ar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ried with them, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 4.2.</ns0:note> and baptized <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>and there he tarried with them, and baptized</ns0:hi> by his Disciples; for himself personally baptized none. But as in our com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mon Speech, so in the Language of Scripture, there is nothing more ordinary than for persons to be said them<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />selves to do, what they do by others, 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 26.11, 12. 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 22.16. 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 34.24. <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 7.51.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:334" />23 ¶ And John also was baptizing in Aenon, near to Salim, <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Aenon</ns0:hi> is here said to be near <ns0:hi>Salim</ns0:hi>; it was the Name of a City, as some think; others say, River or Brook near that City; neither the <ns0:hi>River,</ns0:hi> nor the <ns0:hi>City,</ns0:hi> are elsewhere men<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tioned in Scripture: but <ns0:hi>Topographers</ns0:hi> place it on the <ns0:hi>Eastern</ns0:hi> part of the Lot of <ns0:hi>Manasses,</ns0:hi> not far from <ns0:hi>Bethshan</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Scythopolis</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> because there was much water there <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">there <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> was Baptizing; because this <ns0:hi>Aenon</ns0:hi> was a <ns0:hi>Brook</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>River</ns0:hi> that had much Water, which in <ns0:hi>Iu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dea</ns0:hi> was rare. There is no Water more holy than other. <ns0:hi>Ihon</ns0:hi> Baptized in <ns0:hi>Iordan</ns0:hi> and in <ns0:hi>Bethabara,</ns0:hi> and in <ns0:hi>Aenon.</ns0:hi> The Ordinance sanctified the Water, but did not require <ns0:hi>consecrated</ns0:hi> Water for the due Administration of it. It is from this apparent, that both <ns0:hi>Christ</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> Baptized by <ns0:hi>dipping</ns0:hi> the Body in the Water; else they need not have sought places where had been a great plenty of Water; yet it is probable, that they did not constantly dip, from what we read of the Apostles baptizing in Houses, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 9.17, 18. and 10.47, 48.</ns0:note>: and they came, and were baptized <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">the people came to <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> and were baptized, that is, great numbers of them did so.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 For <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Matth. 14.3.</ns0:note> John was not yet cast into prison <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">For John was yet in the exercise of his publick Mini<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stry: not cast into prison, as he was soon after.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25 ¶ Then arose a question between <ns0:hi>some</ns0:hi> of Johns disciples and the Jews, about purifying <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">The <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> had so many Purifyings, some legal, insti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tuted by God, ordained by <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> as Gods Minister; some <ns0:hi>Traditional,</ns0:hi> brought in by the Pharisees, as their washings before meat, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 15. <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 7. that it seemeth an hard thing to determine, what the Question was betwixt <ns0:hi>Iohns</ns0:hi> Disciples and the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> about what Purifying; and the boldest determiners in this case, are no better than <ns0:hi>guessers</ns0:hi>: some would have <ns0:hi>Baptism</ns0:hi> to be meant here by Purifying. It would much conduce to the resolution of the Question, if we knew what these <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> were, with whom <ns0:hi>Iohns</ns0:hi> Disci<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ples argued. If they were of the <ns0:hi>Pharisees,</ns0:hi> it is probable, the Question was about <ns0:hi>Iohns Baptism,</ns0:hi> considering the frequent washings and purifyings that they had in use amongst them. If they were other <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> the Question might be about the virtue and efficacy of the ceremonial washings, ordained by the Law of God, whether they were mere types, and now to cease? Whether in themselves they conduced any thing to the washing and cleansing of a Soul? If these <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> were (as some think, but I know not how it can be proved) Disciples of Christ, the Question might be, about <ns0:hi>Iohns</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Christs Baptism</ns0:hi>: This Notion seemeth to be favoured by what went before; Where the Evangelist had been speaking of <ns0:hi>Baptism,</ns0:hi> as administred by Christs Disciples, and by <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi>; as also from what followeth, viz. <ns0:hi>Iohns</ns0:hi> Disciples coming to him and, complaining, That Christ by his Disciples baptized more than their Master. But there seemeth to be this great prejudice against the Notion of those learned Men that have imbraced that No<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> That the Question is said to have risen betwixt <ns0:hi>Iohns Disciples and the Iews</ns0:hi>; now we want an instance in Scripture, where the <ns0:hi>Disciples of Iohn</ns0:hi> are put in opposi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion to the Disciples of <ns0:hi>Christ,</ns0:hi> and under Notion of the <ns0:hi>Iews.</ns0:hi> The term <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> generally signifying, that part of the people who adhered to the <ns0:hi>Iudaical Rites</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Religion</ns0:hi>; especially where (as here) it is used in opposition, either to the <ns0:hi>Disciples of Iohn,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>of Christ.</ns0:hi> It is most probable therefore the Question was, either about the <ns0:hi>washings</ns0:hi> or<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dained by the Law of <ns0:hi>Moses,</ns0:hi> or about the <ns0:hi>Traditional wash<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ings</ns0:hi> observed by the Pharisees.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26 And they came unto John, and said unto him, Rabbi <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">The Disciples of <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> coming unto him, give him the usual title, under which in that age, they were wont to speak to those whom they owned as their Teachers, which was <ns0:hi>Rabbi</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, he that was with thee beyond Jor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dan, to whom thou barest witness <ns0:note n="m." place="bottom">Their business was to complain, That <ns0:hi>Christ</ns0:hi> whom they do not think fit to name, nor to give him any title, but mention him as one much inferior to their Master, one that came to him to <ns0:hi>Bethabara,</ns0:hi> and to whom he there gave testimony, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 1.7, 34. as if Christ had from him de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rived all his credit and reputation. Their Master did not go to Christ, but he came to their Master: he was not baptized of Christ, but Christ was baptized of him; he did not give testimony to their Master, but their Master gave testimo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ny to him; now say they</ns0:note>, behold, the same baptizeth, and all men come to him <ns0:note n="n," place="bottom">he baptizeth by his Disciples, and multitudes, many of all sorts of people (for the univer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sal particle <ns0:hi>All men,</ns0:hi> can here signifie no more) come to him; Love is jealous, they were afraid that their Masters reputa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion would by this means flag and be diminished. Such a passage we find, <ns0:hi>Num.</ns0:hi> 11.28. And thus <ns0:hi>Iohn,</ns0:hi> our Saviours Disciple, w<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> jealous for Christ his Master, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 9.49. They all sinned, as appears by the answer given by <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Io<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />shua, Num.</ns0:hi> 11.29. and Christs answer to <ns0:hi>Iohn, Luke</ns0:hi> 9.50. and by the following reply of <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> to these Disciples, en<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vying for his sake.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">27 John answered, and said, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Cor. 4.7. Heb. 5.4. Jam. 1.17.</ns0:note> A man can <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">or, <ns0:hi>Take un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />to himself.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceive nothing, except it be given him from hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">The Ministry, and the <ns0:hi>success</ns0:hi> of the Ministry, must both be given a man from Heaven: Doth he baptize? it is a sign he is sent of God. Do all men come to him? that also is from God. An excellent Corrective of Ambi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion, Envy and Jealousie; no man hath in the Church of God Authority, but he to whom it is given from Heaven; no Authority over his Son.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">28 Ye your selves bear me witness, that I said, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 1.20.</ns0:note> I am not the Christ <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">I appeal to you that are my Disciples, Did not I always plainly tell you, That I was not the Christ? i<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> belongeth unto Christ alone who is the Head of the Church, to send out such as shall labour in it, and to restrain those that labour in it; would you have me silence or suspend him? I told you, that I was but one of his Ministers</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mal. 3.1. Mark 1.2. Luke 1.17.</ns0:note> but that I am sent be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore him <ns0:note n="q," place="bottom">sent before him to prepare his way, <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 1.20, 23.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">29 He that hath the bride, is the bridegroom: but the <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Cant. 5.16.</ns0:note> friend of the bridegroom <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">Christ, whose the Church is by a right of Redemption, and by its having given up its self to him, 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 8.5. He is the Bridegroom of it, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 22.2. 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 11.2. <ns0:hi>Eph.</ns0:hi> 5.23, 25, 26. As his Father was the Husband of the Jewish Church; it belongeth to him to give Laws to it, and to order Mat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ters and Affairs in it.</ns0:note> which standeth, and heareth him, rejoyceth greatly because of the bridegrooms voice <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">I am but as one who is the Friend of the Bridegroom, one of the <ns0:hi>Children of the Bride-cham<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ber,</ns0:hi> Matth. 9.15. and have by my Preaching prepared the People of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> for him; And in stead of being troubled to hear that he is come, I rejoyce greatly to hear his Voice.</ns0:note>: This my joy therefore is ful<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />filled. <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">So far am I from repining to hear that multitudes go to him, that my <ns0:hi>joy is fulfilled,</ns0:hi> (that is) I have no greater Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tisfaction than to hear it.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">30 He must increase <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">In Honour, and Dignity, and Reputation in the World; he is the Rising-Sun (to give you notice of which, I was but as the Morning-Star) he must shine every day more and more.</ns0:note>, but I <ns0:hi>must</ns0:hi> decrease <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">God hath indeed used me as a Prophet, yea more than a Prophet, not to foretell Christ alone, but to point him to you. I have had my time, and finished my Course, and God hath given me a Reputation proportioned to the Work he gave me to do, and to the time in which I was to work; but I must every day decay, and grow less and less, as Christ increaseth, and groweth more and more.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="31">31 He that cometh from above <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 11.15.27.</ns0:note>, is above all <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">He that cometh <ns0:hi>from heaven</ns0:hi> (for it appeareth by the latter part of the Verse, that is the sense of <ns0:hi>from above</ns0:hi>); as Chri<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> did, not only in respect of his Divine Nature, but be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing (as to his whole person) cloathed with Majesty, and Au<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thority from above, infinitely excelleth any one who is a mere Creature</ns0:note>: he that is of the earth, is earthly, and speaketh of the earth <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Cor. 15.47.</ns0:note>: he that cometh from heaven is above all <ns0:note n="y;" place="bottom">he that is of an Earthly Original, speaketh of the Earth. Such as is a mans original, such is hisnature, such is his discourse. Tho I be sent of God, as <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 16.27. and my Baptism be from Heaven: (so our Saviour himself testifieth, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 21.25.) yet my Original is of the Earth, and my Relations and Expressions are suitable to a mere Man: But he that is from Heaven, excells all, as in the digni<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ty of his person, so in the sublimity of his knowledge.</ns0:note>:</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="32">32 And what he hath seen and heard, that he testifieth <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Another great difference which the <ns0:hi>Baptist</ns0:hi> teacheth his Disciples to put betwixt his Testimony and Christs, is, That he, and so all other Ministers of the Gospel, testifie by <ns0:hi>Revelation</ns0:hi>; Christ testifieth not by Revelation, but from his own personal knowledge, what himself hath <ns0:hi>seen</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>heard</ns0:hi> from his Father, see Verse 11. where our Saviour had spoken to <ns0:hi>Nichodemus</ns0:hi> much the same. So <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 1.18. and 8.26. and 15.15. By these two terms is signified the most certain and infallible knowledge of those things which he testified, which made them worthy of all acceptation:</ns0:note>, and no man receiveth his testimony <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">But yet very few received his Testimony, so as to believe in it, see <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 1.11. and <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 11. of this Chapter.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="33">33 He that hath received his testimony <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rom. 3.4.</ns0:note>, hath set to his seal, that God is true <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">He who hath so beleived the testimony of Christ, as to accept him, and to believe in him as his Saviour, hath by that his believing, set to his Seal, that God in all his promises of the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> under the old Testament, is true; that a word hath not failed of whatsoever God hath there spoken of that nature; according to this is that 1 <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 5.10. <ns0:hi>He that believeth not God, hath made him a liar, because he believeth not the Record that God gave of his Son.</ns0:hi> This saying doth notably commend Faith, and defame Unbelief. Faith in Christ as the only true Mediator and Saviour, gi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />veth testimony to the truth of God, and sealeth it. Unbelief defameth God, and doth in effect say, That God is a liar.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="34">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:335" />34 For he whom God hath sent <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">He whom God hath sent out of Heaven, out of his bo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />som, not meerly authorising him as a Minister, as the Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phets, and as <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> was sent</ns0:note> speaketh the words of God <ns0:note n="d," place="bottom">speaking nothing but the words of God. The Prophets, and the Apostles were sent of God, in a sense, but not as Christ was sent; they some<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />times spake the words of God, when the Spirit of God came upon them; but they sometimes spake their own words, as <ns0:hi>Nathan</ns0:hi> did to <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> when he encouraged his thoughts to build an house to the Lord. And <ns0:hi>Paul,</ns0:hi> when he said, <ns0:hi>To the rest speak I, not the Lord</ns0:hi>; but whatsoever Christ spake, was the words of God</ns0:note>: for God giveth not the Spirit by measure <ns0:hi>unto him</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="e:" place="bottom">For God did not give out the Spirit to him sparingly (as out of a measure) as he doth to his Ministers or Saints, who have but their proportion of Revelations and Graces, as was requisite for their Offices to which they were called; and the several periods of time that were gradually illuminated. But in him the fulness of the Godhead dwelt bodily, he was anointed with the oyl of gladness above his fellows: He had the Spring of all in him<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>e<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>f, not the Streams only.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="35">35 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 5.20. So as every man hath reason to <ns0:hi>receive</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>imbrace</ns0:hi> Christ and his <ns0:hi>Testimony,</ns0:hi> and to believe in him.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="36">36 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Habbak. 1.4. Vers. 16. 1 Joh. 5.10.</ns0:note> He that believeth on the Son <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">He that hearing the Proposition of the Gospel, so a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />greeth to it, as with his heart he receiveth him as his Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viour, and trusteth and hopeth in him, <ns0:hi>hath everlasting life</ns0:hi>; that is, a certain and just Title to it, nay in the first fruits; being actually delivered from condemnation, to which, without Faith, he is exposed, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 8.1: He already liveth a spiritual life, <ns0:hi>Gal.</ns0:hi> 2.20. and having Christ in him, hath the hope of Glory; into the possession of which, he shall most certainly come</ns0:note>, hath ever<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lasting life: and he that believeth not the Son <ns0:note n="h." place="bottom">But he that receiveth not the Go<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />spel, published by him who is the Son of God, and doth not imbrace him as his Saviour, and yield obedience to him, shall not be saved. The word here translated, <ns0:hi>believeth not,</ns0:hi> is, <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> which often signifieth, one that is not obe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dient: But <ns0:hi>this is the command of God, That men should be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieve on his Son,</ns0:hi> 1 John 3.23. The commandment doth not only respect <ns0:hi>Love,</ns0:hi> but <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi> in the first place; for <ns0:hi>Faith worketh by Love</ns0:hi>; so as there is an <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, a disobedi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ence in the <ns0:hi>Vnderstanding,</ns0:hi> as well as in the Conversation; and he that so <ns0:hi>believeth not,</ns0:hi> as to <ns0:hi>obey,</ns0:hi> shall never come into Heaven, which felicity is here expressed by <ns0:hi>seeing Life</ns0:hi>; as not seeing Death, is not dying, so <ns0:hi>not seeing Life</ns0:hi> is dying</ns0:note>, shall not see life <ns0:hi>i</ns0:hi>: but the wrath of God abideth on him <ns0:note n="k." place="bottom">And as he was <ns0:hi>by nature a child of wrath,</ns0:hi> Eph. 2.3. subject, and exposed to the wrath of God, so that wrath <ns0:hi>abideth</ns0:hi> upon him, being <ns0:hi>justified by Faith, he hath peace with God,</ns0:hi> Rom. 5.1.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
